prompt:
You are one role in an autonomous ML research agent for KuaiRand-Pure.
The immutable task is within-user ranking of long_view using validation GAUC and nDCG@5.
Use train and validation only. Never request or infer hidden-test information. Do not change
the official evaluator, split, label, budgets, or reference files. Return only the requested
structured output. Evidence must be attributable to a supplied method card or primary source.
Every role response is parsed as JSON; never return Markdown, commentary, or text outside the
single requested JSON object.

EDA roles produce compact planning/report artifacts only. They do not generate candidate.py,
modify raw data, change evaluators, or inspect hidden-test data. Prefer train-only evidence
and leakage-safe feature hypotheses compatible with registered families: bpr, group_softmax, history_features, multi_task.

## Data Quality

- 239 videos with zero duration (24,076 train rows affected)
- 15,609 exact duplicate rows in the training-period log
- Sentinel: is_live_streamer = -124 on 21,127 of 27,285 user rows
- UNKNOWN values: user_active_degree (6), video_type (1), upload_type (80)
- Constant columns: is_lowactive_period, visible_status, is_rand
- hourmin encodes hour times 100 in UTC+8
- The training-period log begins on 20220409, not 20220408

## Feature Coverage

- Video features: 100.000 % of train+valid video IDs found in the feature table
- User features: 100.000 % of train+valid user IDs found in the profile table

## Leakage Flag

The video statistics table is a period aggregate over full-platform traffic.
Implied total shows: 12.83 B vs 2.62 M logged
exposures (ratio approximately 4,892 to one). Observation periods per video
range 45 to 181, exceeding the interaction log span.
Legal for use, but any feature derived from it must be caveated as leaky.

## Metric Conventions

- Task: within-user ranking (each user's impressions ranked against each other)
- nDCG@5: sorts by score with a stable sort (ties fall back to row order)
- AUC: averages ranks over ties (Mann-Whitney U)
- GAUC: per-user AUC, only users with 0 < positives < impressions,
  weighted by positive count
- Zero-positive users: nDCG recorded as 0.0 and included in the average
- Primary score = mean(GAUC, nDCG@5)

## Measured Dead Ends

- Adding all 13 static feature fields: primary 0.5940 vs 0.5950 for the default 5
- Embedding dimension k = 8 / 16 / 32: primary 0.5895 / 0.5902 / 0.5887 (flat)
- The bottleneck is not features or capacity
- First-order user-only terms contribute exactly 0 to within-user ranking
  (any term constant within a user does not change intra-group ordering)


ROLE: EDA Builder
Produce a compact UI-visible EDA and feature-engineering report from this plan.
You may infer only from the supplied DATA CARD and experiment history; do not invent exact statistics that are not present.
Separate observations from implications. Every feature candidate must state implementation scope and leakage risk.
Favor feature candidates compatible with src.models.features, history_features, multi_task, BPR, or group_softmax.
Return concise JSON: at most 3 findings, 3 feature candidates, and 3 UI notes. One sentence per field.

feature_candidates.description: Map tab field (values 0–14) to a learned embedding vector used as a feature in the scoring model, allowing non-linear tab interactions with other features.
feature_candidates.expected_impact: Should directly separate long_view propensity between tabs (e.g., tab 4 vs tab 0), improving GAUC and nDCG@5 without leakage.
feature_candidates.implementation_scope: Add tab to the feature input dict; augment model with embedding table of size ~15×d; integrate in candidate encoder for bpr or group_softmax.
feature_candidates.leakage_risk: None—tab is observed at exposure time and is recorded in both train and validation log rows.
feature_candidates.name: tab_categorical_embedding

feature_candidates.description: For each (user, tab), compute the long_view rate over that user's prior impressions in the same tab (causal, using train log only); optionally include click history.
feature_candidates.expected_impact: Captures user-specific tab affinity and recency, which should sharpen ranking for heavy users (p50=34 rows, p99=219 rows) with no future leakage.
feature_candidates.implementation_scope: Sort train log by user_id and hourmin; build per-user cumulative counters; encode as ratio features (e.g., prior_longview_ratio_tab, prior_click_ratio); feed into feature family history_features.
feature_candidates.leakage_risk: Low if computed strictly from preceding rows per user; must hold out validation from any causal computation and avoid full-train aggregates.
feature_candidates.name: user_tab_history_longview_rate

feature_candidates.description: Discretize video duration into bins (including a dedicated zero-duration flag) to capture non-linear duration–long_view relationship for both positive and negative durations.
feature_candidates.expected_impact: Duration bucket can separate very short/low-quality videos from longer ones, improving ranking especially given the 239 zero-duration videos affecting 24k train rows.
feature_candidates.implementation_scope: Create a categorical feature from video duration via fixed-width or quantile bins; include a binary zero_duration indicator; add to model feature encoder.
feature_candidates.leakage_risk: None—duration is a static attribute of the video known at exposure time.
feature_candidates.name: video_duration_bucket

findings.evidence: DATA CARD Tab Breakdown (train): tab 0=4.22%, tab 1=38.61%, tab 4=48.93%, tab 10=61.25%.
findings.implication: Encoding tab as an explicit categorical/embedding feature should improve within-user ranking because tab strongly separates positive propensity beyond the current baseline.
findings.observation: Train long_view rate ranges from 0.42% (tab 3) to 61.25% (tab 10) and 48.93% (tab 4); tab 1 (73% of rows) has 38.61% rate vs tab 0 at 4.22%.
findings.title: Tab drives long_view rate dramatically

findings.evidence: DATA CARD Label Rates: is_click 46.3447% vs long_view 33.6620% train; Tab Breakdown shows consistent click/long_view ordering.
findings.implication: A multi-task (multi_task family) auxiliary head for is_click may regularize and lift long_view ranking, but only if computed leakage-safe from train; explore as auxiliary signal.
findings.observation: Overall click rate is 46.34% and long_view 33.66%; tabs with higher click rates (e.g., 61.96% in tab 4) also show higher long_view rates, suggesting a click–long_view funnel.
findings.title: is_click strongly correlates with long_view

findings.evidence: DATA CARD Leakage Flag: implied total 12.83 B vs 2.62 M logged, ratio approx 4892:1.
findings.implication: Using any statistic from that table would inflate validation metrics but fail at test time; all new features must be computed from the interaction log only or marked as an explicit ablation.
findings.observation: The video statistics table aggregates 12.83 B exposures vs 2.62 M logged (ratio ~4892:1) and observation periods (45–181 days) exceed the log span, so derived features encode future popularity.
findings.title: Video statistics table leaks future traffic

data.recommended_next_focus: Run a controlled experiment adding the tab categorical embedding to the best group_softmax (temp=2) config, and in parallel prototype the causal user_tab history feature on train to verify its validation GAUC/nDCG@5 gain before integration.
data.summary: EDA on KuaiRand-Pure long_view ranking: tab and within-session position show strong rate variation, causal user-history features are promising and leakage-safe, while the period-aggregate video statistics table leaks future information. Best experiments (group_softmax temp2) plateau near primary 0.6042, suggesting feature/context exploration may yield the next gain.
ui_notes: Show tab×long_view rate table with row shares and confidence bars to highlight strong tab signal.
Display a causal-history validation plot: train-only cumulative long_view rate vs actual long_view on validation for top tabs.
Flag duplicate rows and zero-duration videos counts in UI so users see the cleaning decisions made before feature computation.
